changes.what: OSM nearest-distance algorithm (implementation bug, definitions unchanged)
changes.finding: The V0.7 accumulator (preslide.v07.infrastructure.RunningMinimum) assigns every OSM vertex only to its single nearest sample. A sample whose nearest vertex is even nearer to another sample is never updated and its distance is overestimated, up to the 5000 m cap. On the first full run (both variants streamed together, so most samples appear twice with identical coordinates) the median distance was the cap (5000 m); a 4-sample test reproduces it (samples 10 m and 100 m from a road: V0.7 returns 10 m and 5000 m).
changes.fix: preslide/anfaelligkeit_at_v01/infrastructure.py: every buffered vertex chunk gets its own KD-tree that all samples query; the running minimum is the exact nearest-vertex distance. Building/road definitions, densification (25 m) and the cap (5000 m) are the registered V0.7 ones. Regression test test_nearest_vertex_distance_is_exact_for_clustered_samples with the V0.7 behaviour as injected bug.
changes.use_of_wrong_values: none: the wrong table was overwritten before any analysis used it; the pilot-1 table (40 samples) was also computed with the V0.7 accumulator and is not used
changes.consequence_outside_this_version: V0.7 (frozen, not changed here) used the same accumulator on samples 0.75-10 km apart; its control distances may be overestimated where a positive or another control lies nearer to the same road or building. Reported as a follow-up, not corrected in V0.7.

changes.change: point queries were replaced by polygon queries per 10 km EPSG:3035 tile (native CRS, paged) with the same rule: exactly one covering polygon, else missing
